purpose.en: English movement definitions used by the StreetGym curriculum.

notice.en: These coaching definitions are newly authored for StreetGym.

global_safety.en: Use controlled, pain-free range. Stop for sharp pain, numbness, dizziness, joint instability, or a sudden loss of strength. Skill holds end when body shape changes; do not grind to failure.

description.en: March lightly while swinging the arms and gradually raising body temperature.

safety.en: Keep the pace conversational and land softly.

description.en: Walk at an easy pace to recover while keeping a little daily movement.

safety.en: Use level ground and shorten the walk if fatigue rises.

description.en: Step one foot sideways as both arms arc overhead, then alternate.

safety.en: Stay low impact and keep knees tracking over toes.

description.en: Make slow circles in both directions with relaxed fingers.

safety.en: Use a small range if the wrists feel stiff.

description.en: From hands and knees, gently shift shoulders forward and back over the palms.

safety.en: Keep most weight on the knees and never push into wrist pain.

description.en: Draw slow, controlled circles with straight arms and quiet ribs.

safety.en: Use only a smooth, pinch-free arc.

description.en: Alternate open-and-cross arm swings without forcing end range.

safety.en: Keep the motion loose and below any painful angle.

description.en: Move the spine gently between rounded and extended positions with the breath.

safety.en: Move segment by segment and avoid forcing the low back.

description.en: On hands and knees with one hand behind the head, rotate the upper back to open the elbow toward the ceiling while the hips stay over the knees; breathe slowly.

safety.en: The movement comes from the upper back, not a forced shoulder stretch.

description.en: Trace controlled circles through a comfortable hip range.

safety.en: Hold a support if balance limits the motion.

description.en: Drive the knee gently over the middle toes while the heel stays down.

safety.en: Stop before the heel lifts or the ankle pinches.

description.en: Hold a support and swing one leg front to back with a quiet trunk.

safety.en: Begin with a small arc and avoid snapping the knee.

description.en: From a straight-arm hang, draw shoulders down without bending the elbows.

safety.en: Use a box for partial unloading if the shoulders shrug painfully.

description.en: Keep elbows straight while the shoulder blades glide together and apart.

safety.en: Keep ribs controlled and use an incline if wrists or shoulders complain.

description.en: Perform straight-arm shoulder-blade motion with hands on a secure high support.

safety.en: Verify that the support cannot slide.

description.en: Hang with feet ready to assist and let the grip and shoulders acclimate.

safety.en: Do not sink into a painful shoulder; keep a foot on support when needed.

counts.en: Both hands on the bar, arms straight, feet off the floor the whole time. The time ends when a foot touches or a hand lets go.

description.en: Hold the bar while the feet carry enough weight to maintain comfortable shoulders.

safety.en: Keep the support directly under you and step down before grip fails.

description.en: Maintain straight elbows, shoulders gently down, and ribs stacked over pelvis.

safety.en: End the hold before the shoulders rise uncontrollably.

counts.en: Arms straight, shoulders drawn down away from the ears and kept there, feet off the floor. The time ends when the shoulders rise; a relaxed hang is a dead hang.

description.en: Use only enough leg help to pull the chest toward a low bar with a smooth path.

safety.en: Keep shoulders away from ears and lower under control.

description.en: Step to the top and lower through a controlled range before stepping down.

safety.en: Never jump to a bar blindly; stop the descent before shoulder control is lost.

description.en: Pull from an active hang without kicking, then return to straight arms under control.

safety.en: Leave one or two clean reps in reserve; no neck reaching. If a set comes up short, finish its remaining repetitions foot-assisted.

counts.en: Palms facing away, hands about shoulder width. From a still hang on straight arms, chin over the bar, back to straight arms. No kick or swing, and at most 2 s of rest between reps.

description.en: Pull with palms facing you, a quiet body, and a controlled full descent.

safety.en: Use a grip width that keeps elbows and wrists comfortable.

counts.en: Palms facing you. From a still hang on straight arms, pull until the chin clears the bar, then lower to straight arms. No kick or swing, and at most 2 s of rest between reps.

description.en: Keep a straight body and pull the chest to a secure waist-high bar.

safety.en: Test the bar and footing before leaning back.

description.en: Use a more upright body angle and pull the sternum toward the bar.

safety.en: Keep the feet planted and the bar secure.

description.en: Row a rigid body to the bar while the heels rest on a secure support.

safety.en: Use only a non-slip support and keep hips from dropping.

description.en: Stand tall on straight arms with shoulders gently depressed and feet ready to assist.

safety.en: Step down before elbows bend or shoulders collapse.

counts.en: On parallel bars with locked arms, shoulders pushed down, feet off the floor and touching nothing. The time ends when an elbow bends or the shoulders sink.

description.en: Use the feet to unload a straight-arm support between stable bars.

safety.en: Keep the feet directly beneath you and avoid shoulder pain.

description.en: Descend between bars while the feet provide just enough assistance to press back up.

safety.en: Use a comfortable depth and keep shoulders from rolling forward.

description.en: Start in support, lower slowly to a comfortable depth, then step back up.

safety.en: Stop before the front of the shoulder feels strained.

description.en: Lower with stable shoulders, then press to a tall straight-arm support.

safety.en: Use pain-free depth and keep one or two reps in reserve.

counts.en: From locked arms on parallel bars, lower until the shoulders are below the elbows, then press back to locked arms. No kick or swing, and at most 2 s of rest between reps.

description.en: Hold above a waist-high bar with straight arms, a hollow trunk, and light contact if needed.

safety.en: Use a bar low enough for a safe step-down.

counts.en: On top of a straight bar with locked arms, shoulders pushed down, feet off the floor. The time ends when an elbow bends, the shoulders sink or the feet take weight.

description.en: Keep a straight body and lower the chest to a secure elevated surface.

safety.en: Verify the surface cannot move and keep elbows at a comfortable angle.

description.en: Lower a rigid body to comfortable depth and press the floor away.

safety.en: Keep hips and ribs connected; stop before technique breaks.

counts.en: Hands under the shoulders, body straight from head to heels. Lower until the chest touches the floor or a fist-high marker, then press to locked arms. Rest only at the top, at most 2 s; the set ends at the first rep that sags.

description.en: Pause briefly near the bottom while maintaining a rigid body, then press smoothly.

safety.en: Shorten the pause or elevate the hands if alignment changes.

counts.en: A full push-up with a 2-second stop, chest a fist above the floor and the body straight, then a press to locked arms without a bounce.

description.en: Use a comfortable close hand position and keep elbows tracking back.

safety.en: Do not force a diamond shape if wrists object.

counts.en: Hands closer than shoulder width, elbows brushing the sides, chest to a fist-high marker, then locked arms. Body straight.

description.en: With hips high, bend the elbows and guide the head forward between the hands.

safety.en: Use a short range and an incline if shoulders or wrists feel overloaded.

counts.en: Hands shoulder width, feet walked in until the hips are high over the hands. Lower until the head touches the floor in front of the hands, then press to locked arms.

description.en: Sit between the hips with balanced feet, then stand tall.

safety.en: Use a depth that keeps feet planted and knees comfortable.

description.en: Reach the hips to a stable seat and use light hand support as needed.

safety.en: Use a stable seat that cannot slide.

description.en: Descend slowly, stay balanced, and stand without bouncing.

safety.en: Reduce depth before the pelvis tucks or knees become painful.

description.en: Pause at a stable depth, keep the whole foot grounded, then stand.

safety.en: Use a higher pause position if knees or hips object.

description.en: Step back, lower with a tall torso, and drive through the front foot to return.

safety.en: Hold a support and shorten the step if balance is uncertain.

description.en: Use a staggered stance and light hand support while lowering straight down.

safety.en: Use a short pain-free depth and stable footing.

description.en: Shift toward one leg while the other lengthens, using support for balance.

safety.en: Stay shallow and keep the loaded knee aligned with the toes.

description.en: Rise onto the balls of the feet, pause, and lower with control.

safety.en: Use hand support and keep pressure across all toes.

description.en: Press through the feet and lift the hips without arching the low back.

safety.en: Stop at full hip extension rather than overextending the spine.

description.en: Keep the pelvis level while one leg supplies the bridge effort.

safety.en: Return to two legs if hamstrings cramp or the pelvis twists.

description.en: Maintain a long body line while breathing behind a gently braced abdomen.

safety.en: End the hold when hips sag or the low back feels compressed.

description.en: Hold a straight body with hands on a secure elevated surface.

safety.en: Verify the support cannot move and keep breathing.

description.en: Flatten the low back gently while holding bent knees over the hips.

safety.en: Raise the head or keep it down according to neck comfort; stop if the back lifts.

description.en: Lie on your back, press the low back into the floor and lift the shoulders and straight legs a little off the floor, arms by the ears or by the sides. Hold one long, slightly curved line.

safety.en: Raise the legs higher or bend the knees if the low back lifts. Keep breathing and stop before the neck strains.

description.en: Alternate opposite arm and leg while the trunk stays quiet against the floor.

safety.en: Shorten limb range before the low back arches.

description.en: Reach opposite arm and leg long while keeping hips and ribs square.

safety.en: Reach long rather than high and avoid twisting.

description.en: Support on one forearm and bent lower knee while keeping hips forward.

safety.en: Keep the shoulder stacked over the elbow and stop if it pinches.

description.en: Support on one forearm with the elbow under the shoulder and both legs straight, feet stacked or staggered. Lift the hips into one line from head to heels and hold without rolling forward. Repeat on the other side.

safety.en: Keep the supporting shoulder pushed away from the floor. Return to the knee side plank if the hips sag or the shoulder pinches.

description.en: From an active hang, lift bent knees without swinging and lower slowly.

safety.en: Use short sets and step down before grip or shoulder control fails.

counts.en: From a still hang, lift the knees until the thighs pass hip height, then lower to a straight hang. No swing.

description.en: Draw bent knees toward the trunk while keeping the low back controlled.

safety.en: Reduce range if the low back arches.

description.en: Lower bent legs away from the trunk only as far as the low back stays quiet.

safety.en: Make the lever shorter immediately if the back arches.

description.en: Lift the chest and legs slightly while reaching long through fingers and toes.

safety.en: Think length, not height; stop if the low back compresses.

description.en: Press tall between supports, lighten the feet, and draw knees toward the chest. Once steady, lift both feet off the floor for the last seconds of each hold.

safety.en: Keep feet close to the floor for an immediate exit.

description.en: Roll onto the upper back, stack hips gently, and return without loading the neck.

safety.en: Weight stays on shoulders and upper back, never the neck.

description.en: At a low bar, use the legs to guide chest from below the bar to a straight-bar support.

safety.en: Keep feet grounded, move slowly, and never force wrists over the bar.

description.en: Use a low bar and leg support to rehearse bringing hips toward the bar into support.

safety.en: Use a spotter or keep feet available; do not throw the head back.

description.en: Use a low bar and a small leg drive to pass smoothly into support, then step down.

safety.en: Keep repetitions low, bar path close, and landing controlled.

description.en: Pull the lower chest toward the bar without kicking or craning the neck.

safety.en: Regress once height drops; do not chase the bar with the chin.

counts.en: From a still hang on straight arms, pull until the chest below the collarbones touches the bar, then lower to straight arms. No kick or swing, and at most 2 s of rest between reps.

description.en: Use a securely anchored band to practice a close, symmetrical transition above the bar.

safety.en: Inspect the band, protect the face, and never use a frayed band.

description.en: Pull high, pass both shoulders over together, and finish in stable straight-bar support.

safety.en: Attempt only with prerequisite high pull and dip strength; avoid chicken-wing transitions. Start when ten strict pull-ups, five chest-to-bar pull-ups and ten straight-bar dips are controlled.

counts.en: From a still hang on straight arms, pull and press over the bar to locked arms on top with no kip, swing or kick, then lower back to the hang. At most 2 s of rest between reps.

description.en: Under a low bar, tuck the knees and use light foot contact while drawing the hips upward.

safety.en: Keep feet close, shoulders active, and range small.

description.en: Hold a compact tuck under the bar with active shoulders and hips near shoulder height.

safety.en: Use a spotter or low rings and end before the shoulders lose position.

counts.en: Under the bar on straight arms, knees tight to the chest, back level with the floor. The time starts once the back is level and ends when the hips drop or an elbow bends.

description.en: Open the hip angle from tuck while maintaining a level trunk and active shoulders.

safety.en: Return to tuck immediately when the hips fall or elbows bend. Start when three 10-second tuck holds stay level with the hips at shoulder height.

counts.en: As the tuck front lever, with a flat back and the hips opened until the thighs point straight down from a level trunk. Straight arms; the time ends when the hips drop.

description.en: Extend one leg from an advanced tuck without rotating the pelvis.

safety.en: Alternate legs evenly and regress before the back arches. Start when three 10-second advanced-tuck holds are clean, at least six weeks after your first advanced-tuck practice.

counts.en: One leg straight in line with a level body, the other tucked, arms straight. Hold each leg in turn; your weaker side counts.

description.en: Hold a straight body with legs opened only as wide as needed for control.

safety.en: Use short submaximal holds and avoid lumbar arching. Start when three 8-second one-leg holds on each side are clean.

counts.en: Legs straight and apart, the whole body level with the floor, arms straight. The time ends when the hips drop or a knee bends.

description.en: Maintain a straight horizontal body under the bar with locked elbows and active shoulders.

safety.en: Stop as soon as the line breaks and return to the straddle. Start when a previous class has completed three clean 8-second straddle holds. Through Level 6 it appears only as a single readiness check; Level 7 trains brief one-to-three-second holds and Levels 8-10 lengthen them, always with the straddle in the same class as the fallback.

counts.en: Legs straight and together, the body one straight line level with the floor, arms straight. The time starts once the line is level and ends when it breaks.

description.en: With low rings or a low bar and feet available, rotate only through a comfortable shoulder range.

safety.en: Never force a German hang; reverse direction before any shoulder stretch becomes intense.

description.en: On low rings or a low bar with the feet on the floor, rotate back through a partial skin-the-cat until the hands are behind you. Let the shoulders open only as far as is comfortable and hold, keeping the feet in contact for support.

safety.en: Never force the range: the stretch should stay mild in the front of the shoulders and biceps. Keep the feet supporting you, come out the way you went in, and stop for sharp shoulder or elbow pain.

description.en: From a supported inverted tuck, lower only slightly toward a tucked back-lever line.

safety.en: Set up on low rings or a low bar with the feet on the floor or a box, as in the German hang, and unload the feet only as far as control allows. Use a spotter if available. Shoulder extension stays pain-free; no forced depth.

description.en: Hold a compact tuck behind the bar with straight elbows and controlled shoulders.

safety.en: Set up on low rings or a low bar with the feet on the floor or a box, as in the German hang, and unload the feet only as far as control allows; use a spotter if available. Stop before shoulder extension feels strained. Start when skin-the-cat and tuck entries are smooth and pain-free in the shoulders and elbows.

counts.en: Facing down behind the bar on straight arms, knees tight to the chest, back level with the floor. The time ends when the hips rise or drop or an elbow bends.

description.en: Open the hips from tuck while retaining straight elbows and a level trunk.

safety.en: Regress immediately if shoulder comfort or elbow lock changes. Start when three 10-second tuck holds are clean and the elbows and biceps feel nothing the next day.

counts.en: As the tuck back lever, with a flat back and the hips opened until the thighs point straight down from a level trunk. Straight arms.

description.en: Extend one leg from advanced tuck while keeping hips square.

safety.en: Set up over a box or with the feet near the floor, as in the German hang, so the feet can take weight at any moment, and unload them only as far as control allows; use a spotter if available. Alternate sides and keep holds brief. Start when three 10-second advanced-tuck holds are clean.

counts.en: Facing down, one leg straight in line with a level body, the other tucked, arms straight. Hold each leg in turn; your weaker side counts.

description.en: Extend into a straight straddle line behind the bar with controlled shoulders.

safety.en: Use submaximal holds and stop at the first loss of shoulder position. Start when three 8-second one-leg holds on each side are clean.

counts.en: Facing down, legs straight and apart, the whole body level with the floor, arms straight.

description.en: Hold a straight horizontal line behind the bar with locked elbows.

safety.en: Use a safe exit and stop as soon as the line breaks or the shoulders feel strained, then return to the straddle. Start when a previous class has completed three clean 8-second straddle holds. Through Level 6 it appears only as a single readiness check; Level 7 trains brief one-to-three-second holds and Levels 8-10 lengthen them, always with the straddle in the same class as the fallback.

counts.en: Facing down, legs straight and together, the body one straight line level with the floor, arms straight. The time starts once the line is level and ends when it breaks.

description.en: Anchor the shoulders, keep weight off the neck, and lower a bent-knee body line slowly.

safety.en: Shoulders and upper back bear contact; never load the neck or lose low-back control.

description.en: Lower with one leg longer while maintaining a single rigid line from shoulders through hips.

safety.en: Alternate legs and stop before the hips fold or back arches. Start when three sets of three bent negatives keep the hips open.

description.en: Lower a straight body slowly from the shoulders while gripping a secure anchor.

safety.en: Never place pressure on the neck; regress as soon as body line bends. Start when three sets of two one-leg negatives per side are smooth.

description.en: Raise and lower a rigid body from shoulder support without hinging at the hips.

safety.en: Use low repetitions, a secure anchor, and zero neck pressure. Start when three sets of two slow full negatives are smooth.

counts.en: Shoulders on a bench, hands holding behind the head. Lower the straight body until it is just above the bench and raise it back to vertical, at least 2 s down, with no bend at the hips.

description.en: Hold a long body line with hands on a secure support and shoulder blades gently spread.

safety.en: Keep the support fixed and set an angle that is painless for wrists.

description.en: From a protracted plank, shift shoulders slightly beyond the hands while keeping elbows straight.

safety.en: Increase lean by millimetres, not ego; stop for wrist or elbow discomfort.

counts.en: Straight arms, a straight body and the shoulders a hand's length past the wrists, measured against the same floor line every time. The time ends when the lean shrinks or an elbow bends.

description.en: Balance knees lightly on the upper arms with hands planted and a cushion ahead.

safety.en: Practice low, look slightly forward, and keep a clear padded fall zone.

counts.en: Hands on the floor, knees resting on the bent arms, both feet off the floor. Bent-arm balance: the straight-arm tuck planche is its own skill.

description.en: With straight elbows and protracted shoulders, lift tucked feet from the floor.

safety.en: Use parallettes if wrists prefer neutral grip and stop before elbow lock changes. Start when three 20-second planche leans with pushed-away shoulders are clean.

counts.en: Straight arms, knees tight to the chest, feet off the floor, hips level with the shoulders. The time starts once the feet lift and ends when they touch or an elbow bends.

description.en: Open the hips from tuck while shoulders stay protracted and elbows remain straight.

safety.en: Regress on any wrist, elbow, or anterior shoulder discomfort. Start when three 8-second tuck planche holds are clean.

counts.en: As the tuck planche, with a flat back and the hips opened, the trunk level with the floor and the hips at shoulder height. Straight arms.

description.en: Hold a straight-arm horizontal position with the legs opened for leverage.

safety.en: Attempt only after repeatable advanced-tuck holds; keep efforts brief and submaximal. Start when three clean 8-second advanced-tuck holds are repeatable. Through Level 7 it is a single readiness check; Levels 8-10 train it, with the advanced tuck in the same class to step back to.

counts.en: Straight arms, legs straight and apart, the whole body level with the floor and the feet off it.

description.en: Hold the body horizontal on straight arms with no foot support.

safety.en: Attempt this only after long-term prerequisite development; otherwise perform the listed regression for the assigned sets. Start when two clean 5-second straddle holds are repeatable. Levels 9-10 train it, with the straddle in the same class to step back to.

counts.en: Straight arms, legs together, the body one straight line level with the floor. The time ends when the hips drop, a knee bends or a foot touches.

description.en: With a soft elbow, lightly extend or flex the wrist until a mild stretch appears. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: No bouncing, tingling, or strong pull.

description.en: Hold a secure support, send hips back, and breathe into the sides of the ribs.

safety.en: Keep shoulders comfortable and avoid hanging bodyweight from the arms.

description.en: Place the forearm on a support and turn away slightly while breathing calmly. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: Keep the elbow below a painful angle and use only mild tension.

description.en: Tuck the pelvis gently and shift forward until the front of the rear hip stretches mildly. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: Pad the knee and avoid arching the low back.

description.en: Hinge from the hips over a slightly bent leg while holding a support. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: Keep the spine long and avoid nerve-like tingling.

description.en: Hold support, bring one heel gently toward the seat, and keep knees close. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: Do not pull the ankle hard or arch the back.

description.en: Keep the rear heel down and lean forward gently into a wall. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: Keep the foot pointing forward and use mild tension.

description.en: Sit hips back toward heels and rest the arms or chest on support while breathing slowly.

safety.en: Widen knees or raise the support for knee and hip comfort.

description.en: Let bent knees drift slightly to one side while shoulders stay relaxed. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: Use a small range and stop for back or hip pain.

description.en: Breathe quietly through the nose with a slightly longer exhale.

safety.en: Return to normal breathing if light-headed.

description.en: Shift gently to one side until the inner thigh lengthens, keeping the supported foot flat. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: Use a comfortable range and never bounce into the stretch.

description.en: Crawl with knees hovering low, opposite hand and foot moving together, and the trunk quiet.

safety.en: Take short steps and stop if the wrists or lower back lose a comfortable position.

description.en: Hold a post if needed, sit into a comfortable deep squat, and keep the whole foot grounded.

safety.en: Reduce depth if the heels lift or the knees feel pinched.

description.en: From an active hang, alternate a small hollow and arch shape without bending the arms.

safety.en: Keep the swing small and shoulder-led; do not chase height or kick aggressively.

description.en: Begin in straight-bar support and lower slowly through the transition into a controlled hang.

safety.en: Use a safe way into support and stop before the shoulders roll forward or one side drops first. Start when six strict pull-ups and six straight-bar dips are controlled; until then do the foot-assisted low-bar pullover for the same sets.

description.en: Sit in a 90/90 position and lean forward gently over the front shin with a long spine. Each timed set is for one side; alternate sides between sets. If there is an odd number of sets, start on the other side next session.

safety.en: Support the hands and reduce the angles if either knee feels uncomfortable.

description.en: Rotate both knees from one 90/90 side to the other under control; each arrival counts as one alternating repetition unless the workout explicitly says per side.

safety.en: Place the hands behind the body when needed and use only a pain-free range.

description.en: From a stable support, take short alternating hand steps along the parallel bars.

safety.en: Keep shoulders depressed, steps short, and feet ready to land safely.

description.en: Lean shoulders slightly beyond the hands and perform a controlled push-up while keeping the body rigid.

safety.en: Turn the hands only as comfortable, limit the lean, and stop for wrist or front-shoulder pain.

counts.en: Hands by the hips with the fingers turned out, shoulders ahead of the hands by the same lean every rep (mark it on the floor). Chest to just above the hands, press to locked arms keeping the lean. A rep that loses the lean doesn't count.

description.en: Place the whole foot on a stable step, stand tall through that leg, and lower with control.

safety.en: Use a low stable surface and prevent the working knee from collapsing inward.

description.en: From straight-bar support, lower the chest toward the bar and press to a stable lockout.

safety.en: Use only a controlled depth that keeps both shoulders comfortable and level.

counts.en: From locked arms on a straight bar, lower until the bar meets the lower chest, then press back to locked arms. No kick or swing. Parallel-bar dips count as dips, not here.

description.en: Keep a straight body line, lower the chest toward a wall, and press away smoothly.

safety.en: Use secure footing and keep elbows at a comfortable angle from the torso.

description.en: Slide the arms upward against a wall while keeping ribs quiet and shoulders comfortable.

safety.en: Use a smaller range rather than arching the lower back or forcing the shoulders.

description.en: Hold a secure support and descend on one leg only as far as balance and knee control allow.

safety.en: Keep the knee aligned with the foot and use the support rather than twisting.

description.en: Perform a controlled single-leg squat while the free leg reaches forward and the working heel stays grounded.

safety.en: Use only a depth that preserves foot pressure, knee alignment, and balance. Start when three sets of eight assisted pistols per leg are controlled.

counts.en: On one leg with the free leg straight in front and the heel down. Lower until the hip is below the knee, then stand to a straight leg without touching anything. Your weaker leg counts.

description.en: From an active hang, raise straight legs without swinging and lower with trunk control.

safety.en: Bend the knees or stop the set when the back arches or grip fades.

counts.en: From a still hang, lift straight legs until the feet pass hip height, then lower to a straight hang. No swing.

description.en: Raise the feet toward the bar from a controlled active hang without a kip, then lower slowly.

safety.en: Use a smaller range before swinging begins and step down before grip failure.

counts.en: From a still hang, lift the legs with the knees straight until the toes touch the bar, then lower to a straight hang. No kip or swing between reps.

description.en: Stand tall with ribs stacked over pelvis. Reach both arms overhead without arching the back; gently elevate the shoulders. This rehearses the handstand line with feet grounded.

safety.en: Use only comfortable overhead range. Keep breathing; this is preparation, not a loaded handstand.

description.en: Lie on one side, elbow below shoulder and knees bent. Lift hips into line with shoulders and knees; hold without rolling. Repeat on the other side.

safety.en: Keep the supporting shoulder active. Shorten the hold or keep hips down if needed.

description.en: Place feet on a stable box and hands on the floor. Bend at the hips into an L shape, straighten elbows and push the floor away. Bring shoulders toward the hands only while you can step down calmly. Use a lower box and bent knees if needed; keep the head off the floor.

safety.en: Use the easier variation until wrists and shoulders tolerate it comfortably. Keep elbows straight and breathe. Before inversion, rehearse a controlled exit with a qualified coach or spotter; never kick up without an exit.

description.en: From a plank facing away from a clear wall, walk feet up and hands in only as far as you can reverse safely. Push tall with straight elbows and ribs tucked. Walk back down before fatigue. A partial wall walk is valid.

safety.en: Use the easier variation until wrists and shoulders tolerate it comfortably. Keep elbows straight and breathe. Before inversion, rehearse a controlled exit with a qualified coach or spotter; never kick up without an exit.

counts.en: Chest to the wall, arms locked, body straight, only the toes on the wall. The time ends when the elbows bend or you come down.

description.en: From a controlled chest-to-wall handstand, shift pressure through the fingertips until the toes briefly become light. Return to light wall contact. The time is a practice window, not a required unsupported hold.

safety.en: Use the easier variation until wrists and shoulders tolerate it comfortably. Keep elbows straight and breathe. Before inversion, rehearse a controlled exit with a qualified coach or spotter; never kick up without an exit. Start when three 40-second chest-to-wall holds feel calm and you can walk down or cartwheel out at will.

description.en: From a chest-to-wall handstand, shift your weight into one hand, turn the hips to the side and step down one foot at a time, finishing like the end of a cartwheel. Practise both directions until the exit happens without thinking.

safety.en: Clear the floor around you and use a mat. Keep the elbows straight and look at the floor between the hands. Start with small turns close to the wall, and learn the exit with a qualified coach or spotter before balance attempts.

description.en: Near a clear wall, make low-effort entries and brief balance attempts using the exit already rehearsed with a coach. Reset between attempts. The time is a practice window; return to wall balance work whenever needed.

safety.en: Use the easier variation until wrists and shoulders tolerate it comfortably. Keep elbows straight and breathe. Before inversion, rehearse a controlled exit with a qualified coach or spotter; never kick up without an exit. Start when 10-second toe pulls are calm, kick-ups to the wall are controlled and the cartwheel exit is automatic.

counts.en: Your longest clean balance in the practice window: both feet off the wall and the floor until a foot comes down. Resets and kick-ups between attempts are not hold time.

description.en: Kick up away from the wall and hold a straight, stacked handstand: hands shoulder-width, shoulders open over the hands, ribs in and legs together. Balance with the fingers and come down with the rehearsed exit.

safety.en: Warm the wrists first and practise only with a clear exit and space around you. Start when ten-second balances away from the wall are repeatable.

counts.en: No wall: straight body, locked arms, hands staying where they landed (finger corrections are fine, steps are not). One continuous hold, ended by a foot coming down or a hand moving.

description.en: Stand beside a fixed vertical support and take a comfortable wide split grip. Keep both feet down and lean slightly away to rehearse upper-hand pulling and lower-hand pushing. Reverse sides.

safety.en: Use fixed stall bars or a rated flag pole, never a loose rail or door frame. Train both sides. Keep the lower arm straight, push with the lower hand and pull with the upper hand. Stop for elbow or shoulder discomfort; do not jump into the hold.

description.en: Use fixed stall bars with a secure low foothold. From split-grip support, bring knees toward the chest while retaining firm foot assistance. Lift only enough to practise the sideways body line; lower under control. Without a foothold or spotter, use grounded support.

safety.en: Use fixed stall bars or a rated flag pole, never a loose rail or door frame. Train both sides. Keep the lower arm straight, push with the lower hand and pull with the upper hand. Stop for elbow or shoulder discomfort; do not jump into the hold. Start when three 15-second grounded flag supports on each side are solid.

description.en: Only after assisted holds and controlled exits are repeatable, briefly unload the foothold with knees tucked. Keep the trunk facing forward and shoulders active. Regain foot support before form changes. Longer-leg and full flags come after stable tuck control, not after finishing a level.

safety.en: Use fixed stall bars or a rated flag pole, never a loose rail or door frame. Train both sides. Keep the lower arm straight, push with the lower hand and pull with the upper hand. Stop for elbow or shoulder discomfort; do not jump into the hold. Start when three 8-second assisted tuck flags on each side are solid.

counts.en: Side-on to the pole, arms straight, knees tucked, the trunk level with the floor. Hold each side; your weaker side counts.

description.en: From a solid tuck flag, open both legs into a wide straddle for a brief sideways hold, then tuck again and lower under control. Keep the trunk facing forward and the hips in line with the shoulders.

safety.en: Use fixed stall bars or a rated flag pole, never a loose rail or door frame. Train both sides. Keep the lower arm straight, push with the lower hand and pull with the upper hand. Return to the tuck before the hips drop. Start when three 5-second tuck flags on each side are solid.

counts.en: Side-on to the pole, arms straight, legs straight and apart, the body level with the floor. Hold each side; your weaker side counts.

description.en: From the straddle flag, bring the legs together into one straight sideways line for a brief hold, then return to the straddle or the tuck. It starts as a single readiness check; the last phase of Level 7 trains it as brief holds with the straddle flag in the same class.

safety.en: Use fixed stall bars or a rated flag pole, never a loose rail or door frame. Train both sides. Keep the lower arm straight, push with the lower hand and pull with the upper hand. Start when three 5-second straddle flags on each side are solid; if the line breaks, use the straddle flag.

counts.en: Side-on to the pole, arms straight, legs straight and together, the body one line level with the floor. Hold each side; your weaker side counts.

description.en: From a wide overhand hang, pull toward one hand while the other arm stays nearly straight along the bar. Lower under control, then pull to the other side; repetitions are per side.

safety.en: Keep both shoulders packed and the straight elbow soft. Use pull-ups instead once the chin no longer clears the bar without twisting. Start only when about ten strict pull-ups feel controlled.

counts.en: Hands about twice shoulder width. Pull to the working hand while the other arm stays straight along the bar and only guides; lower to straight arms. Your weaker side counts.

description.en: From a wide overhand hang, pull up toward one hand, slide the chin along the bar to the other hand while staying at the top, then lower under control. Alternate the starting side; repetitions are per side.

safety.en: Keep both shoulders packed and the elbows soft; the slide stays level, without kicking or twisting. Return to archer pull-ups as soon as the chin drops below the bar during the slide. Start when three sets of five archer pull-ups per side are controlled.

counts.en: Pull up to one hand, slide the chin along the bar to the other hand without dropping below it, then lower to straight arms. Each pull counts for the side it starts on; your weaker side counts.

description.en: Hang from the bar with one hand and hold a towel looped over the bar, or a light band, low with the other hand. Pull up mainly with the bar arm, using the towel hand only as much as needed, then lower under control. Repetitions are per side.

safety.en: Keep the working shoulder packed and the elbow in front of the body, and stop at any elbow or shoulder pain. Move the towel hand lower only when every repetition is smooth, one change at a time. Start when three sets of three typewriter pull-ups per side are smooth.

description.en: Step up from a box to the top position with both hands, let go with one hand and lower with the working arm as slowly as you can control, about four to six seconds, until the arm is straight. Step down and reset; repetitions are per side.

safety.en: Use the box to reach the top so the working arm only lowers. Keep the shoulder packed through the whole descent and stop if the elbow or shoulder hurts or the descent turns into a drop. Start when three sets of three assisted one-arm pull-ups per side are controlled.

description.en: Hang from one hand with the shoulder packed and the free hand on the chest. Pull until the chin clears the bar without kicking or twisting toward the bar, then lower under control to a straight arm; repetitions are per side.

safety.en: Start when one-arm negatives of five seconds per side are smooth, three a side. Keep the shoulder engaged from the dead hang, never drop into a straight arm, and stop if the elbow or shoulder hurts.

counts.en: One hand on the bar, palm facing away, the free hand on the chest and off the arm. From a still hang on a straight arm, chin over the bar, back to a straight arm. No kick or twist. Your weaker side counts.

description.en: From a wide push-up, lower toward one hand while the other arm slides out nearly straight. Press back to the middle, then lower to the other side; repetitions are per side.

safety.en: Keep the body in one line and the working elbow about 45 degrees from the ribs. Shorten the range or return to push-ups if the hips sag. Start only when about twenty strict push-ups feel easy.

counts.en: Hands about twice shoulder width. Lower toward the working hand while the other arm stays straight and only guides, then press back up. Your weaker side counts.

description.en: Feet wide, one hand under the shoulder and the other behind the back. Lower the chest to fist height with the body in one line and the hips square, then press back up; repetitions are per side.

safety.en: Start when five archer push-ups per side are clean. Keep the working elbow close to the ribs and the hips level; raise the hand on a bench if the hips twist.

counts.en: Feet no wider than shoulder width, the free hand behind the back, hips and shoulders square to the floor. Chest to fist height, then a locked arm. Your weaker side counts.

description.en: With the feet on a stable box and the hips stacked high over the hands, lower the head forward of the hands toward the floor, then press back to straight arms.

safety.en: Use a box that cannot slide, let the elbows travel back rather than flare, and stop before the head touches the floor. Return to floor pike push-ups if the hips drop.

counts.en: Feet on a box at about hip height, hips stacked over the hands. Lower until the head touches the floor in front of the hands, then press to locked arms.

description.en: From a chest-to-wall handstand, lower slowly until the head lightly touches a folded mat, then walk the feet down the wall to exit. Reset standing instead of pressing back up.

safety.en: Requires a calm 30-second chest-to-wall handstand and a practised walk-down exit. Keep a folded mat under the head and never drop onto the head or neck.

description.en: From a chest-to-wall handstand, lower the head to a folded mat under control and press back to straight arms, then walk down the wall to exit.

safety.en: Start only after five controlled four-second negatives. Keep the repetitions few and crisp, exit by walking down, and stop at any neck discomfort.

counts.en: Chest to the wall, hands shoulder width. Lower until the head touches the folded mat, then press to locked arms. Legs straight and still: no kick.

description.en: With the hands on two low parallettes or stable blocks in a chest-to-wall handstand, lower the head below hand level toward a folded mat under control, press back to straight arms, then walk down the wall to exit.

safety.en: Keep the deficit small at first and the blocks stable. Lower only as deep as the shoulders stay comfortable, keep the elbows tracking forward and stop at any neck or shoulder discomfort. Start when three sets of five wall handstand push-ups are smooth.

counts.en: As the wall handstand push-up, with the hands on blocks or parallettes about 10 cm high, so the head lowers below the hands to the mat. Press to locked arms with no kick.

description.en: Kick up to a freestanding handstand a short step from a clear wall, then lower slowly, elbows tracking forward, until the head lightly touches a folded mat. Tuck the knees and step the feet down instead of pressing back up; the wall is only a backstop.

safety.en: Practise with a mat and a cartwheel exit that is already automatic. Lower in three to five seconds, never drop onto the head or neck, and cartwheel out early whenever balance drifts. Start when three sets of three deficit wall handstand push-ups are smooth and a 5-second freestanding hold is repeatable.

description.en: Support on straight arms on parallel bars or blocks with one leg straight forward at hip height and the other knee tucked. Hold the listed time on each leg, switching legs within the set.

safety.en: Keep the arms locked and the shoulders pushed down. Return to the tuck L-sit if the hips sink behind the hands. Start after three clean 15-second tuck L-sits with both feet off the floor.

counts.en: Locked arms, one leg straight at hip height or higher with the heel off the floor, the other tucked. Hold each leg in turn; your weaker side counts.

description.en: Support on straight arms with both legs straight together at hip height, toes pointed and shoulders pushed down away from the ears.

safety.en: Keep holds short and the shape exact; bend one knee as soon as the legs drop. Start after three clean 10-second holds on each leg in the one-leg version.

counts.en: Locked arms, both legs straight and together at hip height or higher, heels off the floor.

description.en: From an L-sit, push the shoulders down and lean them back while lifting the straight legs above hip height into a V, toes pointed.

safety.en: Start when twenty-second L-sits are clean. Keep the arms locked and hold only as high as the hips allow; stop for wrist or elbow pain.

counts.en: Locked arms, both legs straight and raised at least 45 degrees above level, the feet about head height or higher. Below that it is an L-sit.

description.en: Sit tall with the legs straight together and the hands flat beside the knees. Lift both heels a few centimetres using the hip flexors and abdominals, pause, then lower slowly.

safety.en: Keep the knees straight and the chest lifted; a small lift is enough. Lift one leg at a time if the hip flexors cramp.

description.en: With the rear foot on a knee-high bench or box behind you, lower the back knee toward the floor over the front foot and drive up through the front heel. Repetitions are per leg.

safety.en: Use a stable bench, keep the front knee tracking over the toes, and hold a post for balance when needed.

description.en: Lie on your back with the heels on a towel or sliders and lift the hips into a bridge. Slide the heels out until the legs are nearly straight, then curl them back in while the hips stay high.

safety.en: Use a smooth floor, keep the hips lifted throughout, and shorten the slide if the hamstrings cramp.

counts.en: Heels on sliders or a towel, hips up. Slide both legs out nearly straight, then curl the heels back under the knees with the hips staying up.

description.en: Kneel on a mat with the heels anchored under a low bar or held by a partner. Keep the hips extended and lower the torso forward as slowly as possible, catch the floor with the hands, then push back up to kneeling.

safety.en: Use padding under the knees and a secure anchor, catch the floor early, and keep repetitions few. Expect hamstring soreness at first; do not add repetitions until it settles.

description.en: A readiness check, not a target: kneel with the heels anchored, keep the hips extended and lower slowly through the full range, then pull yourself back up with the hamstrings, using only a light push from the hands if needed.

safety.en: Use padding under the knees and a secure anchor. Start when two sets of eight Nordic negatives are controlled. Make each repetition a controlled attempt; if the pull back up fails, finish it as a negative.

counts.en: Knees on a pad, heels held. Lower the straight body from knees to head under control to the floor, then pull back up with the hamstrings alone. A push from the hands is good training, but only unassisted reps count here.

description.en: Stand on one leg with a soft knee and hinge at the hip so the torso and free leg move together toward horizontal, then drive the hip forward to stand tall. Repetitions are per leg.

safety.en: Keep the hips square and the back long. Touch a wall or post lightly for balance and hinge only as far as the back stays neutral.

description.en: Lie face down with the forehead on a towel. Lift straight arms into a Y, then a T, then bend them into a W, drawing the shoulder blades back and down. One repetition is one full Y-T-W sequence.

safety.en: Keep the neck long, the thumbs pointing up and the lifts small and slow.

description.en: From a half squat, jump straight up, land softly through the whole foot with the knees tracking over the toes, and reset before the next jump.

safety.en: Jump on a firm, non-slippery surface, keep the jumps submaximal and quiet, and stop when landings get loud or the knees cave in.

description.en: Stand in a lunge facing a clear wall, hands down about a hand's width from it. Kick up to a back-to-wall handstand, touch the heels to the wall softly, then come down the way you went up. Alternate the lead leg; repetitions are per side.

safety.en: Kick only as hard as the heels need to reach the wall softly, with the elbows locked and the eyes on the floor between the hands. Come down the way you went up, or cartwheel out if you overbalance. Start when two 45-second chest-to-wall holds and the cartwheel exit on both sides are calm.

description.en: Kneel on all fours with the hands flat under the shoulders and the fingers pointing forward. Press the heels of the hands off the floor until you are on the fingers and knuckles, pause, then lower slowly. Finish the set with the hands turned over, backs of the hands on the floor, rocking gently forward and back over them. One repetition is one lift or one rock.

safety.en: Keep most of the weight on the knees at first and move only as far as is comfortable; shift more weight onto the hands over the weeks. Stop for sharp wrist pain.

description.en: Face a wall or a bar at chest height, hands on it shoulder-width apart and arms straight. Walk the feet back and hinge at the hips, letting the chest sink between the arms until the arms line up with the trunk. Keep the ribs pulled in and breathe slowly through the hold.

safety.en: Feel the stretch in the armpits and upper back, not the lower back: keep the ribs down and the back flat. Ease off for any pinching at the front of the shoulder.

description.en: Sit tall in a wide straddle with the knees and toes pointing up and the hands on the floor beside the knees. Lean forward from the hips with a long back, then lift both heels a few centimetres by squeezing the front of the hips. Pause, lower slowly and lean a little further each repetition.

safety.en: Fold from the hips rather than rounding the back; a small lift is enough. Lift one leg at a time if the hip flexors cramp.

description.en: Sit on the ground with the upper back against the front edge of a bench, the edge just below the shoulder blades, hands cradling the head (never pulling on the neck) and elbows forward. Breathe out and arch the upper back over the edge, keeping the hips on the ground, pause for two seconds, then return.

safety.en: Move from the upper back only: keep the ribs down and the lower back still. Pad the edge with a towel, and stop if the neck strains.
